The Plan in Short

Thirty-Six Islands in the Arabian Sea. Our Loop Visits a Few of Them.

Ten of the islands are inhabited, and the rest are sandbanks and coral. We fly from Kochi to Agatti and stay on three islands: Kavaratti, Agatti and Thinnakara, with a day visit to little Kalpitti. Scroll down and the camera follows us day by day, and every day opens into full details.

Permit and Island Transfers

Tourist Permit Advisory

As shown on the official e-Permit portal: people travelling to Lakshadweep for a holiday should apply under the Tourist category. Sponsorship is no longer required, and a Police Clearance Certificate no longer has to be uploaded for Tourist category applications.

Entry Permit (e-Permit)
  1. Create an account on the official e-Permit portal and sign in.
  2. Choose the Tourist category and list the islands: Agatti, Kavaratti, Kalpitti and Thinnakara. Visitors can only go to islands named on the permit.
  3. Upload a photo ID and a passport-size photo, and add travel dates and stay details.
  4. Pay the fee online. Travel sites report about ₹250 per adult (₹50 application and ₹200 heritage fee).
  5. Track the application, then keep a printed and a digital copy of the approved permit.

Every one of the seven of us needs a permit. Travel sites advise applying at least 14 days before travel, and approved permits are generally valid for up to 30 days. The portal's notice says all e-Permit services move to a new portal from 15 October 2026, so always start from the official link.

Getting Between the Islands

Kochi to Agatti. Flights run on small turboprops, and Agatti has the only airstrip in Lakshadweep. Our Day 1 flight is Alliance Air 9I-505.

Agatti to Kavaratti. Kavaratti has no runway. In the fair season, October to May, the crossing is by speedboat and takes about 2 to 2.5 hours. In the monsoon a helicopter takes over, subject to availability.

Agatti to Thinnakara. About 45 minutes by speedboat, roughly 8 km northeast. The resort arranges it.

Crossings between islands run on vessels approved by the Lakshadweep administration, so they are booked through the package operator rather than picked up on the day. The two days to confirm timings are Day 1, when the flight lands at 10:30 and the boat to Kavaratti follows, and Day 6, when the flight leaves at 13:05.

Weather, Flights and Buffers

December sits inside the October to April best season, and the sea is usually calm. Boats and flights can still be delayed by weather, so keep the last day flexible and avoid non-refundable plans on the mainland side.

Small turboprops have strict baggage limits. A 15 kg checked bag and a 7 kg cabin bag are typical, but read the allowance on the ticket.

Money, Signal and the Reef

Carry enough cash for tips and small purchases, as card and UPI acceptance can be patchy. Mobile data is often slow, so download tickets, permits and maps before leaving Kochi.

Liquor is not permitted on the islands we are visiting. Dress modestly in villages and near mosques.

Do not stand on or take coral or shells, use reef-safe sunscreen, and carry your rubbish back with you.
